summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening dyspnea, generalized weakness, and a mechanical fall. He presented with acute on chronic heart failure, evidenced by elevated proBNP of 6,932 and bilateral pleural effusions. He developed Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia leading to sepsis, likely originating from a focal pyelonephritis in the transplanted kidney, and was treated with meropenem. A scalp lesion was biopsied and diagnosed as squamous cell carcinoma. He experienced a transient ischemic attack with transient dysarthria. Due to worsening renal function and fluid overload, he required temporary hemodialysis with a tunneled catheter placement. He showed clinical improvement with antibiotic therapy, diuresis, and supportive care, and was discharged home with plans for continued IV antibiotics, outpatient dialysis, and follow-up with specialists.
